ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The center of the figure below is the North Pole, the large circle represents the 50° latitude circle, the numbers in the figure indicate longitude degrees, and the areas between P and Q and between M and N are land. Read the figure and answer the following question. <image1> If at point P sunrise happens to coincide with sunset at point Q, then at this time, do ships sailing from west to east in the North Indian Ocean encounter following current or adverse current?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: The figure is a circular schematic diagram centered on the North Pole, and the large circle represents the 50°N latitude circle; there is a cross mark near the center of the circle. On the circumference, P can be seen at the lower-left position, Q at the lower-right position, N at the upper-left position, and M at the upper-right position; near the circumference on the right side is marked “180°”. The stem states that the areas between P and Q and between M and N are land.
Then reason: According to the diagram and the distribution of land near the 50°N latitude, P—Q can correspond to the western and eastern ends of the Eurasian continent near 50°N, with a longitude difference of about 120°, and Q is east of P. The local time difference between the two places is 120°÷15°/hour=8 hours. The question states “when point P has sunrise, point Q happens to have sunset”; for areas at the same latitude, the time from sunrise to sunset is the daytime length, so the daytime length at 50°N at this time is about 8 hours. The daytime length at 50°N is only 8 hours, indicating that the Northern Hemisphere has short days and long nights, and it is winter in the Northern Hemisphere. In winter, the North Indian Ocean is affected by the northeast monsoon, and the monsoon current generally flows from east to west. Ships sailing from west to east in the North Indian Ocean are opposite to the current direction, so they encounter adverse current.
